status.en: 186 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 20% fewer than the week before, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 186 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 20 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Gunmen continue to abduct civilians and attack security forces across northern Nigeria, including the kidnapping of a Plateau university student, two visually impaired persons in Plateau, and 14 schoolchildren from a farm, while killing police officers in Borno, Plateau, Sokoto-Gusau and ambushing a convoy in Zamfara. Bandits also abducted mourners on the Benue highway, a husband and five others in Benue, and worshippers in Kaduna, and killed five police officers heading to a Zamfara APC primary. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpnede menn fortsetter å bortføre sivile og angripe sikkerhetsstyrker i Nord-Nigeria, inkludert bortføringen av en universitetsstudent fra Plateau, to synshemmede personer i Plateau og 14 skolebarn fra en gård, samtidig som de drepte politifolk i Borno, Plateau, Sokoto-Gusau og overfalt en konvoi i Zamfara. Banditter bortførte også sørgelige på Benue-veien, en ektemann og fem andre i Benue, og tilbedere i Kaduna, og drepte fem politifolk på vei til en APC-primær i Zamfara. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
